text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today to $129.35, extending a two-week gain of 3.26%. The move reflects growing concern about oil supply disruptions: Iran has stepped up attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are also threatening crude exports. These geopolitical risks have pushed global oil prices to $113.96 per barrel (compared to a lower US domestic price of $96.16), and traders are pricing in the risk that a critical chokepoint for energy shipments could tighten supply further.

The broader context matters here: supply fears had eased earlier in the week thanks to Middle East crude exports and an emergency stockpile release, but the escalation in tanker attacks has reversed that sentiment. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher global oil prices and renewed supply anxiety generally support the stock, even though US domestic crude is trading at a notable discount to world prices.
